body: Large language models (LLMs) serve users whose cultural identities are multi-layered, yet cultural evaluations commonly reduce identity to one label. In this work, we study LLMs under simultaneous identity cues, with a country persona in the system prompt and a second identity signaled in the user turn, either by naming a country (explicit cue) or through the query language (implicit cue). We test World Values Survey (WVS) multiple-choice probing and open-ended sociopolitical generation. In multiple-choice probing, language cues shift answers about three times more than explicit cues but away from the associated country's distribution, and explicit cues do not consistently move answers toward the named country. Across 1.6 million open-ended responses, naming a country closes 30-44% of the gap to the model's own responses for that country, and explicit cues produce more differentiated value changes than language cues. Our results suggest that country and language cues should be evaluated as distinct signals rather than interchangeable proxies for culture.
summaryZh: 调查法学硕士中的多文化价值选择偏差。大型语言模型（LLM）为具有多层次文化身份的用户提供服务，但文化评估通常将身份简化为一个标签。在这项工作中，我们在同步身份提示下研究法学硕士，在系统提示中显示国家角色，并在用户轮流中通过命名国家（显式提示）或通过查询语言（隐式提示）发出第二个身份信号。
